content.text: Changed to "View Product" — the route goes to `ProductView` (the stocked product item), not product knowledge, so "View Details" was ambiguous. Added the `view_product` key to [en.json](public/locale/en.json#L6602).
List out more such suggestions

Alternatives for the label, given the target is the `ProductView` page (a specific stocked product with batch/expiry/price):

| Label | Why it works | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|
| **View Product** (current) | Matches destination exactly; short | Slightly generic in a product-heavy table |
| **Product Details** | Mirrors existing `product_details` key already in en.json; no new key needed | Drops the verb; less action-like |
| **View Batch** | Most specific — the row is really a batch/lot with expiry + price | Only accurate when a lot number exists |
| **View Item** | Distinguishes the inventory *item* from the product *knowledge* | "Item" is vague without context |
| **Details** | Shortest; column header "Actions" supplies context | Ambiguous when the row name is also clickable (opens deliveries drawer) |
| **Open** | Very short, clearly navigational | Too terse for screen readers |
| **View Stock Item** | Unambiguous vs. product knowledge | Long for a table cell |

Recommendation: keep **View Product**, or drop to **Details** with `aria-label="View product details"` if you want the column narrower. Note the row's product name button opens the deliveries drawer rather than navigating, so keeping a verb on this button helps signal the two are different destinations.

content.text:
Reviewed the diff. Nothing broken — it compiles and the only reported error ([InventoryList.tsx](src/pages/Facility/services/inventory/InventoryList.tsx#L148-L152)) is pre-existing and unrelated. Findings, roughly by priority:

**1. Dead `stopPropagation`** — [InventoryList.tsx](src/pages/Facility/services/inventory/InventoryList.tsx#L311)
`TableRow` has no `onClick`, so `onClick={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}` on the `Link` guards nothing. It made sense when the link sat next to the drawer-opening button; now it's noise.

**2. `w-12` is wider than needed and only a hint** — `TableCell` is `p-2` (8px each side) and the icon is `size-4` (16px), so content is 32px, not 48px. Also the table is auto-layout inside `overflow-x-auto`, so `w-*` acts as a minimum rather than a fixed width. For a true shrink-to-fit column, `w-px` is the idiomatic Tailwind trick; otherwise `w-10` matches the content exactly.

**3. Empty header cell** — `<TableHead className="w-12"></TableHead>` gives screen-reader users an unlabeled column. Either add an `sr-only` label or keep it empty but self-close it (`<TableHead className="w-12" />`) for consistency with the rest of the file.

**4. Icon semantics** — `l-external-link-alt` conventionally signals "opens in a new tab / leaves the app", but this is an in-app raviger navigation to the product page. `l-arrow-right`, `l-eye`, or `l-angle-right` would set a more accurate expectation.

**5. Discoverability trade-off (design call, not a bug)** — moving the link out of the name cell means the product name now *only* opens the deliveries drawer, and the sole navigation affordance is a 16px unlabeled icon at the far right of a 7-column table. That's a small target and easy to miss; the other tables in this feature (e.g. [DeliveryOrderTable.tsx](src/pages/Facility/services/inventory/externalSupply/components/DeliveryOrderTable.tsx#L116-L134)) use a labeled `Button variant="outline"` with an icon. Worth confirming this table is intentionally more compact.

**6. Locale is clean** — `view_product` was reverted and isn't referenced anywhere, so no orphan key for `knip` to flag. `view_product_details` is still used by the `sr-only` span.

w-px is required?

Not strictly required, but it does something: the `Table` is `w-full`, so with no width hint the browser distributes leftover space across all columns — the icon column would get a share of that padding. `w-px` makes it shrink to content and hands the slack to the text columns.

It's only needed on one cell per column though — the browser takes the column's width from the strongest constraint, conventionally the header. I'll drop the redundant one on the body cell.
